transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-01-13 10:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Sam (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Novus ML), Priya (Novus Security), Liam (Novus Infra), Sofia (Novus Product)

Summary: Quick sync on networking and routing updates, review of last week's perf runs, planning for upgrade/rollback plan and stress test. Action items captured at end.

[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight — agenda is networking updates, perf run review, and then upgrade/rollback plan. Sam will cover the run details.
[00:23] Jordan (Customer): Hey, thanks. Quick note — we've got Liam and Priya here to cover infra and security Qs.
[00:30] Sam (SE): Cool. Recap from last week: we completed the initial VPC peering and an internal smoke test. We saw stable connectivity, initial inference tests at 2k requests/hr with average token p95 around 160ms, p99 at ~320ms on the small pilot config. Some noise on cold-starts when the KV cache warmed up.
[01:05] Liam: I saw those logs. One thing — the route table we pushed last week put our app subnet behind a NAT gateway which added a bit of egress latency, we think. We can move the Redwood workers into a private subnet with egress through a dedicated ENI to reduce hops.
[01:30] Sam: Yeah that matches our traces; egress through the nat added ~40-60ms on some calls. If you can do an ENI attachment and update the route this week we can re-run and expect better p95.
[01:50] Priya (Security): For context, we need to confirm KMS usage. Are you using customer-managed KMS keys or Redwood-managed? Also we want to ensure audit logs for model loads and key usage are preserved for SOC2 mapping.
[02:10] Maya (SE): For the pilot we're in a mixed mode: model artifacts are stored in your S3 with encrypted at rest and we can configure Redwood to use your KMS key via IAM role. We'll send the exact policy we need. Audit logs are available and we can forward them to your CloudTrail.
[02:35] Priya: Ok that's good; we need the policy matrix. Also curious about HSM options — we have FIPS requirements for one dataset.
[02:50] Sam: We support HSM for root keys and can integrate with customer HSM vendors; that setup is heavier but doable for the regulated dataset. We'll add HSM checklist to the runbook.
[03:10] Jordan: On perf: last week's 2k/hr number is fine but product wants to see higher throughput. What's the expected scale if we bump batch sizes?
[03:25] Sam: Preliminary tests with batching of 8 improved throughput ~2.6x but increased tail latency; with batching of 4 it's a good compromise — throughput ~1.8x and p99 stayed under 380ms. We can tune batch window but need to consider user-perceived latency SLO.
[03:50] Sofia (Product): Our SLO is 500ms p99 for interactive features, so sounds okay if p99 stays under that. For background workloads we can accept higher tail.
[04:05] Liam: One ops item — during the last upgrade we saw the kernel module for the optimized attention kernels didn't load on one node, caused fallback to slower path. How do we handle that for the planned upgrade?
[04:25] Sam: Good call. For upgrades we recommend canary + health checks per host. Our upgrade runbook will: drain one host, run the kernel install + unit tests, run synthetic inference checks, then promote. If issues we can rollback via image revert. We'll include exact commands and logs to look for.
[04:50] Jordan: Did you catch anything in the last run about KV cache invalidation or duplication? One of our queries showed repeated context in outputs.
[05:05] Maya: That was likely due to a mismatch in sequence id handling when we replayed logs. Noted as a race in the prefix cache; we pushed a small fix to avoid double-insert. We'll push a hotfix to the pilot cluster later today and re-run the failing trace.
[05:30] Priya: From a security perspective, what about access controls on the Redwood console? We need SSO, RBAC scoped to teams, and audit trail for who did rollouts.
[05:45] Alex: We support SAML SSO and granular RBAC. For pilot we can set up a Novus group mapping with least privilege and grant a small set of admin rights to your infra team. Audit logs include rollout events and user IDs.
[06:05] Priya: Great. Please send the SAML metadata and the mapping doc.
[06:12] Sam: We'll attach that in the runbook bundle.
[06:20] Liam: For the stress test on the 20th — what's the test plan? Can you outline concurrency, payload sizes, and which metrics you'll capture?
[06:33] Sam: Sure. Plan: three phases. Phase 1: warm-up with steady 2k/hr for 10m. Phase 2: ramp to 12k/hr over 15m with batching variations (1,4,8). Phase 3: sustained peak for 10m. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, GPU utilization, context switch rates, KV cache hit ratio, and token/sec. We'll also stream logs to your logging endpoint.
[07:00] Jordan: Will you need us to open ports between subnets?
[07:05] Sam: We'll need the Redwood workers to reach your S3 endpoint and the KMS endpoint. If you provide the CIDR we'll send the list of IPs to whitelist. We prefer using VPC endpoints for S3 and KMS to avoid public egress.
[07:20] Liam: We can do VPC endpoints; we also want to peer with the Redwood management control plane for metrics and upgrades. Any constraint on peering vs private link?
[07:35] Maya: Both work; PrivateLink reduces blast radius and is preferred for regulated setups. We'll document the pros/cons in the runbook. For the pilot we set up a peering but can move to PrivateLink if you want the extra isolation.
[07:55] Priya: PrivateLink would be better for our audit posture. Let's plan for that in long-term topology.
[08:05] Alex: Noted. Next, upgrade window — proposed 2027-01-19 02:00 UTC to apply runtime patch and attention-kernel update. Canary in first hour, full rollout in 3 hours if green. Any blackout windows?
[08:25] Liam: We're fine with that window; product will be warned. Priya: need a test that proves rollback works.
[08:35] Sam: We'll run a simulated rollback in staging and capture metrics. We can share the run of that test after we complete it.
[08:45] Jordan: For billing/packaging discussion — any changes to cost when moving from hosted to private?
[08:55] Alex: Private pricing includes reserved capacity for dedicated GPU pools — you'll see different unit economics; we'll send a revised pricing sheet reflecting the pilot's expected usage.
[09:10] Sofia: Sounds good, please share that along with the runbook.
[09:20] Maya: Quick note — we've added a network troubleshooting checklist to the runbook covering route tables, security groups, endpoint configs, and NAT/ENI guidance.
[09:30] Priya: Perfect. A couple of clarifying Qs on logging: do you keep model input logs by default? We need to mask PII.
[09:45] Sam: By default we can redact inputs; for audit you can enable full logs but we recommend token-sampling and redaction rules. We'll include the redaction config options.
[09:58] Alex: Ok wrapping up — recap of next steps: Sam to share runbook + network diagram and SAML metadata by Jan 15; Liam to provide CIDR by Jan 17; schedule stress test Jan 20; Priya to send SOC2/KMS questions by Jan 18. Any other items?
[10:20] Jordan: That's all from us, thanks.
[10:25] Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links.

References and links mentioned: runbook (will be shared), network diagram (diagram link placeholder), pricing spreadsheet (link placeholder), compatibility checklist for KMS/HSM (doc placeholder).

End of transcript.
